_about: Pieces of the history of the land, written for WyrmHex (original text). The engine builds a cast from the building blocks: a realm of old (a realm_kinds entry plus a made-up name from 'names', or a realm_named entry), a long-dead great ruler (titles + made-up name + epithets), the founding people (peoples), two factions of today (faction_kinds + faction_emblems), a forgotten god (made-up name) and a time (years). It then picks one of three forms (a chronicle, the present first and then the past, a told legend) and one line from each sentence list, at random but always the same for the same seed, filling the placeholders: {land}, {years}, {god}, {realm_*}, {ruler_*}, {people_*}, {fac1_*}, {fac2_*} (and {fac_*} in 'faction' lines), {name} and {hex} for sites, {n} for the number of rivers. Italian gets articled forms (_il, _di, _a, _da, _in: 'il Regno', 'del Regno'...) and an agreement ending (_o: o/a for singulars, i/e for peoples), so that no sentence needs to guess a gender; English uses the plain form for all of them and never _o. Rumours are [text, needs], where needs is null or the kind of site the rumour is about (city, fortress, dungeon, river_site).

fortress_intro: Le fortezze di {land} risalgono quasi tutte ai tempi {realm_di}, e oggi sono in mano a chi è riuscito a prenderle.

Le vecchie fortezze sono l'ultimo baluardo contro le terre selvagge, anche se i loro comandanti pensano più ai pedaggi che alla difesa.
Torri, rocche e castelli punteggiano {land} come i denti rotti di una bocca antica, e ognuno ha una storia di assedi e tradimenti.
fortress: {name} ({hex}) sorveglia le vie che portano verso le terre selvagge, con una guarnigione sempre troppo piccola e sempre mal pagata.

dungeon_intro: Sotto {land} si aprono cripte, miniere e templi dimenticati, e ognuno custodisce un frammento della storia {realm_di}.
Le rovine e i sotterranei di {land} attirano avventurieri da ogni dove: pochi ne tornano ricchi, molti non ne tornano affatto.
Ogni villaggio di {land} conosce almeno un luogo dove non bisogna andare, e ogni villaggio ha qualcuno che ci è andato lo stesso.
Il passato di {land} non è sepolto abbastanza in profondità: in molti luoghi affiora, e qualche volta si muove.

dungeon: {name} ({hex}): un tempo la tesoreria {realm_di}; i custodi ne murarono l'ingresso quando tutto crollò, restando chiusi dentro.

{name} ({hex}): qui fu sepolto vivo un re, insieme a tutto il suo seguito e a un tesoro che nessuno ha mai osato reclamare.
{name} ({hex}): i minatori fuggirono in fretta, e gli attrezzi sono ancora dove li lasciarono, accanto a una vena di un metallo senza nome.
{name} ({hex}): un tempio scavato a rovescio nella roccia, sacro a un dio che non vuole essere nominato.
{name} ({hex}): si dice che vi portino i viandanti rapiti sulle strade vicine, e che nessuno di loro sia mai tornato a raccontarlo.

sea: Il mare bagna {land}, e i suoi pescatori raccontano di isole che compaiono e scompaiono con la nebbia.
Lungo le coste di {land} si nascondono calette di contrabbandieri e relitti di navi antiche, ancora carichi di merci che nessuno ha reclamato.
Il mare che bagna {land} è freddo e agitato, e nelle notti di tempesta i marinai giurano di sentire campane suonare sotto le onde.
Dal mare arrivano in {land} mercanti, pirati e notizie di terre lontane, e spesso è difficile capire chi sia chi.
Le scogliere di {land} sono punteggiate di fari spenti, e i pescatori evitano le acque profonde dove, si dice, dorme qualcosa di enorme.
rivers: {n} fiumi scendono dai rilievi verso valle, e lungo le loro rive si concentrano villaggi, mulini e guai.

one_river: Un solo fiume attraversa {land}, ed è la sua via più sicura: chi se ne allontana se ne pente.
Un unico grande fiume divide {land} in due, e le genti delle due rive parlano dialetti diversi e si guardano in cagnesco.
Un solo fiume bagna {land}, e tutta la vita si stringe lungo le sue rive: lontano dall'acqua ci sono solo pietre, vento e ossa.
Un fiume lento e scuro attraversa {land}, e i barcaioli non lo navigano mai di notte, per ragioni che preferiscono non spiegare.
L'unico fiume di {land} nasce da una sorgente che nessuno ha mai visto, e ogni primavera porta a valle oggetti di una città sconosciuta.
no_river: Nessun fiume attraversa {land}: l'acqua viene da pozzi profondi e cisterne antiche, e chi le controlla ha in mano la vita di tutti.
In {land} non scorrono fiumi, e ogni goccia di pioggia viene raccolta con cura in vasche, otri e canali scavati nella roccia.
{land} non ha fiumi, ma i vecchi raccontano che un tempo ce n'era uno, e che fu prosciugato da una maledizione.
Senza fiumi, {land} vive di sorgenti e di pozzi, e le liti per l'acqua sono più aspre di quelle per l'oro.
factions_intro: Oggi in {land} si contendono il potere diverse fazioni, e due di loro contano più di tutte le altre.
Nessun re governa {land}, ma il vuoto lasciato dalla corona è stato riempito da fazioni avide e ambiziose.
Chi vuole fare affari in {land} deve sapere chi pagare, a chi obbedire e a chi non voltare mai le spalle.
Dietro ogni pedaggio, ogni impiccagione e ogni festa di {land} c'è la mano di una delle sue fazioni.
Le vere potenze di {land} non siedono su un trono, ma in sale segrete, locande fumose e accampamenti nei boschi.
In {land} il potere non si eredita: lo si compra, lo si ruba o lo si conquista con la spada, e oggi lo tengono in pochi.
Fra le rovine di ciò che fu {realm_il} si muovono oggi nuove forze, decise a prendersi tutto quello che resta.
faction: {fac_il} riunisce i mercanti più ricchi di {land}, e vuole riaprire le vecchie strade commerciali a qualunque costo.
{fac_il} è nat{fac_o} fra i reduci di una guerra dimenticata, e oggi vende le sue spade a chiunque possa pagarle.
{fac_il} custodisce i segreti dei maghi {realm_di}, e non permette a nessuno di studiarli senza il suo permesso.
{fac_il} predica il ritorno dell'antico dio {god}, e raccoglie seguaci fra i poveri, i malati e i disperati di ogni villaggio.
{fac_il} sostiene di discendere {ruler_da}, e rivendica il diritto di governare {land} in nome dell'antica corona.
{fac_il} controlla il contrabbando di sale, armi e reliquie, e ha orecchie in ogni locanda e in ogni porto.

{fac_il} raccoglie i ladri, i mendicanti e i tagliaborse delle città, e impone le sue regole dove le guardie non arrivano.

{fac_il} presta denaro a signori e villaggi, e riscuote i debiti con una pazienza infinita e una crudeltà ancora maggiore.
{fac_il} protegge i viandanti sulle strade in cambio di un pedaggio, e chi rifiuta di pagare scopre presto da chi lo stava proteggendo.
{fac_il} è guidat{fac_o} da una veggente cieca, e prende ogni decisione leggendo il volo dei corvi e le viscere dei pesci.
{fac_il} recluta giovani nei villaggi più poveri, promettendo terre e titoli in un regno che deve ancora nascere.
{fac_il} studia le rovine e i sotterranei di {land}, e paga bene gli avventurieri che riportano libri, mappe e oggetti strani.
{fac_il} controlla le miniere e le fucine di {land}, e decide chi può comprare armi e chi deve accontentarsi di bastoni.

{fac_il} è temut{fac_o} in tutta {land} per i suoi assassini, che non mancano mai il bersaglio e non lasciano mai testimoni.
{fac_il} gestisce le locande e le stazioni di posta lungo le strade, e sa sempre chi viaggia, con chi e con quanto denaro.

{fac1_il} deve una somma enorme {fac2_a}, e il giorno della scadenza si avvicina senza che ci sia oro per saldare il debito.
Un matrimonio dovrebbe presto unire i capi {fac1_di} e {fac2_di}, ma molti, da entrambe le parti, farebbero di tutto per impedirlo.
{fac1_il} accusa {fac2_il} dell'assassinio del suo vecchio capo, e ha giurato vendetta pubblicamente, davanti a cento testimoni.
{fac1_il} e {fac2_il} hanno firmato una tregua fragile, che regge solo per paura di un nemico comune.
{fac1_il} ha infiltrato le proprie spie fra le file {fac2_di}, e conosce ogni sua mossa prima ancora che venga decisa.
{fac1_il} e {fac2_il} si contendono lo stesso tesoro perduto, ma la mappa per trovarlo è strappata in due, e ne hanno mezza per parte.
Un tempo {fac1_il} e {fac2_il} erano un'unica fazione, e la loro separazione fu così sanguinosa che nessuno ne parla volentieri.
{fac1_il} tiene in segreto un ostaggio prezioso {fac2_di}, e lo usa per ottenere ciò che vuole senza mai alzare la voce.
{fac1_il} disprezza {fac2_il} in pubblico, ma ogni mese, in segreto, ne compra armi, veleni e informazioni.

now_intro: Oggi, però, qualcosa sta cambiando, e anche i più testardi fra gli abitanti di {land} cominciano ad accorgersene.
Ma la fragile quiete di {land} sta per finire, e i segni sono ormai sotto gli occhi di tutti.
Negli ultimi mesi, però, nelle locande di {land} si parla sottovoce di una cosa sola.
Quest'anno l'inverno è arrivato presto, e insieme al gelo è arrivato qualcosa che nessuno sa ancora nominare.
Da qualche tempo, però, i vecchi di {land} scuotono la testa e dicono che il peggio deve ancora venire.
Ora un nuovo pericolo minaccia {land}, e le vecchie rivalità potrebbero presto sembrare poca cosa.
In {land} le cose non restano mai ferme a lungo, e anche questa volta una tempesta si prepara lontano dagli sguardi.
Ma da quando è cominciata questa primavera, in {land} niente va più come dovrebbe.
Ed è proprio adesso, mentre i potenti litigano per le briciole, che su {land} si addensa la minaccia più grave da secoli.
threat: Un esercito di orchi si raduna ai confini, e le sue staffette sono già state viste aggirarsi fra le alture.

I raccolti non crescono più vicino alle antiche rovine, e gli animali fuggono senza motivo verso le terre basse.
Un drago è stato visto volare basso sopra {land}, e da allora le greggi scompaiono una dopo l'altra.
Un erede {realm_di} è riapparso e reclama {land} per sé, con un sigillo che pochi possono contestare e un esercito che cresce ogni giorno.
Le campane di un tempio sepolto suonano di notte, e chi le sente sogna sempre lo stesso sogno.

Il culto di {god} è rinato in segreto, e i suoi fedeli rapiscono viandanti per un rito che deve compiersi al prossimo solstizio.
Un'orda di predoni, cacciata dalle proprie terre da qualcosa di peggiore, sta scendendo su {land} bruciando tutto ciò che incontra.
Un mago folle ha preso possesso di una torre dimenticata, e da allora il cielo sopra {land} cambia colore ogni notte.
La sorgente da cui dipendono i villaggi più grandi si sta prosciugando, e chi controlla l'acqua rimasta potrà dettare legge a tutti.
Un esercito straniero, guidato da un generale che si dice invincibile, ha varcato i confini e chiede la resa di ogni città.
Qualcosa si è svegliato sotto le montagne: la terra trema ogni notte, e dai pozzi sale un'acqua calda che sa di ferro.
Un branco di licantropi caccia nelle campagne di {land}, e qualcuno dice che il loro capo siede di giorno in un consiglio cittadino.
La tomba {ruler_di} è stata profanata, e chi l'ha fatto ha portato via qualcosa che avrebbe dovuto restare sepolto per sempre.
Una nebbia innaturale avanza ogni giorno di qualche passo, e i villaggi che inghiotte non mandano più notizie.
Un gigante sceso dai ghiacciai ha preso dimora in una vecchia fortezza, e pretende un tributo di bestiame da tutti i villaggi della valle.
Un veleno lento ha cominciato a uccidere i potenti di {land} uno dopo l'altro, e ognuno accusa i propri rivali.
Le stelle sopra {land} si sono spostate, e gli astrologi annunciano che il ritorno di {god} è questione di settimane.
Una febbre dell'oro ha travolto {land}: si dice che in una valle remota l'oro affiori dal terreno, e tutti i disperati ci stanno correndo.
Le porte di una fortezza dei nani, chiuse da secoli, si sono riaperte, ma ciò che ne esce non sono nani.
omen: Da tre notti la luna sorge rossa come il sangue, e i cani ululano senza sosta fino all'alba.
Le statue {ruler_di} nelle piazze dei villaggi hanno cominciato a piangere lacrime nere.
Nei pollai nascono pulcini con tre zampe, e le streghe dei villaggi si rifiutano di dire che cosa significhi.
Gli stormi di corvi volano tutti nella stessa direzione, e nessuno li ha mai visti tornare indietro.
In ogni pozzo di {land} l'acqua è diventata salata nello stesso giorno, alla stessa ora.
Una cometa dalla coda verde attraversa il cielo da settimane, e gli astrologi hanno smesso di uscire di casa.
I bambini di {land} cantano nel sonno una filastrocca che nessuno ha insegnato loro, in una lingua morta da secoli.
Sulle porte delle case è comparso in una sola notte un segno tracciato col gesso: il simbolo dimenticato di {god}.
Il vino inacidisce nelle botti, il latte caglia nei secchi e le candele si spengono da sole appena cala il buio.
Un vecchio stendardo {realm_di}, sepolto da secoli, è stato visto sventolare sulla torre più alta di {land}, e nessuno sa chi l'abbia issato.
Le api hanno abbandonato gli alveari e i pesci risalgono i torrenti al contrario, come se fuggissero da qualcosa.
I vecchi sognano tutti, ogni notte, la stessa porta di bronzo, e al risveglio hanno le mani sporche di terra.
In tutta {land} le campane hanno suonato da sole a mezzanotte, tredici rintocchi, e poi hanno taciuto.
Un'eclissi che nessun astronomo aveva previsto ha oscurato il sole per un'ora intera, e da allora i cavalli rifiutano di uscire dalle stalle.
Un pellegrino morente è giunto al villaggio più vicino ripetendo un solo nome, sempre lo stesso: quello {ruler_di}.

forest: Le foreste coprono gran parte di {land}: sono antiche, fitte e piene di sentieri che non portano da nessuna parte.
Nei boschi di {land} vivono ancora creature più antiche degli uomini, e i taglialegna lasciano offerte di pane prima di abbattere un albero.
Le foreste di {land} nascondono fra gli alberi le rovine di città intere, inghiottite dalle radici in pochi secoli di abbandono.
Chi entra nelle foreste di {land} senza una guida perde presto il sentiero, e a volte anche il ricordo di come ci è arrivato.
hills: Le colline di {land} sono punteggiate di tumuli e di torri crollate, e i pastori evitano di salire sulle cime.
Fra le colline di {land} si nascondono valli strette e villaggi isolati, dove gli stranieri sono accolti con il pane e guardati con sospetto.
Le colline di {land} sono traforate da vecchie miniere, e di notte dalle gallerie abbandonate giunge il rumore di picconi che nessuno impugna.
Sulle colline di {land} sorgono cerchi di pietre erette, e i pastori giurano che le pietre cambiano posto da un anno all'altro.
mountains: Le montagne di {land} sono alte e fredde, e i loro passi restano chiusi per metà dell'anno.
Fra le montagne di {land} si aprono passi stretti e ghiacciai antichi, e nel ghiaccio si scorgono a volte figure immobili che sembrano guardare.
Le montagne di {land} sono ricche di ferro e d'argento, e i nani che un tempo le scavavano non hanno mai accettato di averle perdute.
Sulle vette di {land} nidificano aquile grandi come cavalli, e i montanari sanno che chi ne ruba un uovo non scende più a valle.
plains: Le pianure di {land} sono vaste e ventose, e da lontano si vede chi arriva molto prima che arrivi.
Le pianure di {land} sono coperte di grano selvatico e di tumuli erbosi, e l'aratro porta spesso alla luce elmi, ossa e monete antiche.
Sulle pianure di {land} corrono branchi di cavalli selvaggi, e i nomadi che li inseguono non riconoscono confini né padroni.
Le pianure di {land} furono campo di battaglia per secoli, e in certe notti d'autunno vi si sentono ancora i corni e il galoppo.
desert: Il deserto si mangia ogni anno un po' di più di {land}, e sotto la sabbia affiorano tetti e campanili.
Nel deserto di {land} i pozzi sono pochi e gelosamente custoditi, e chi ne conosce la posizione vale più di un carico d'oro.
Le dune di {land} si spostano con il vento, e ogni tempesta scopre e ricopre le rovine di una città che nessuno ha mai trovato due volte.
Nel deserto di {land} il sole uccide di giorno e il freddo di notte, e fra le rocce si nascondono predoni e serpenti grandi come alberi.
swamp: Le paludi di {land} sono nebbiose e piene di insidie, e le loro acque restituiscono a volte ciò che hanno inghiottito.

{realm_il} fell when a dragon claimed the crown's treasure for itself, and none of the knights who rode out to win it back ever returned.
{realm_il} fell when the dead stopped staying in their graves and marched, in silence, against the cities of the living.
After the death of {ruler_il} the heirs fought over the throne for thirty years, and {realm_il} crumbled into a dozen warring lordships.
{realm_il} was swept away by a horde from the north, which burned every library and every temple in its path.
A winter that lasted nine years buried {realm_il} under the snow, and when the thaw finally came there was hardly anyone left to see it.
{realm_il} fell at the hands of a court counsellor who poisoned the rulers and their heirs, then vanished, taking the crown's seal with him.
The priests of {god} cursed {realm_il} from the top of their towers, and from that day no child was ever born within its borders.
{realm_il} borrowed from the mountain dwarves to pay its armies, and when it could no longer settle the debt the dwarves came to collect in person.
The earth shook for three days and three nights, and when it stopped the capital of {realm_il} had sunk into a bottomless chasm.
{realm_il} surrendered without a fight to an army of sorcerers, who ruled {land} for a century through terror and magic.
A revolt of slaves and starving peasants set the cities of {realm_il} ablaze, and the nobles fled beyond the mountains with whatever they could carry.
{ruler_il} sought immortality in forbidden books, and {realm_il} paid the price of that search, down to the last soul.
One day the sun rose red and stayed red for a whole year: the crops withered, the wells ran dry and {realm_il} faded away with them.
{realm_il} was betrayed by its own allies, who opened the gates of the capital to the enemy in exchange for gold and land.
fall_after: The cities were abandoned in haste, and the houses were left with tables laid, cradles empty and chests still locked.
The survivors scattered to the four winds, taking with them only the names of their ancestors and a few family heirlooms.
The crown's treasure vanished in the chaos, and since then generations of seekers have chased it from ruin to ruin.
Within a few years the woods took back the fields, and the paved roads vanished under grass, moss and roots.
The surviving nobles shut themselves inside their castles, and each of them claimed to be the rightful heir of {realm_il}.
The libraries burned, and with them were lost the names of the kings, the maps of the mines and the words to command dragons.
For a whole generation nobody dared to approach the fallen capital, and those who did came back white-haired and speechless.
The last legions of {realm_il} were left without pay or orders, and turned into raiding bands that plundered the very lands they had defended.
The bells of every tower rang for a day and a night, then fell silent, and nobody has heard them ring together since.
The seal of {realm_il} was broken into seven pieces, entrusted to seven families who swore not to join them again until the time was right.
The court wizards sealed their towers from within, and nobody knows whether anyone is still alive behind those doors.
Those who could fled towards the sea or beyond the mountains; those who stayed soon learned to hide in the woods and to trust nobody.
For years the crows were the only masters of the walls, and in {land} people still say “rich as a crow” of anyone who profits from another's ruin.
after: Since then {land} has been no-man's-land: whoever lives here obeys the nearest sword and pays tribute to whoever wields it.
Since then {land} has been a frontier, where settlers come in waves and vanish in waves, leaving no trace.
Since then the people of {land} have mistrusted strangers, wizards and old roads, and they make no secret of it.
Since then {land} has gone wild again, and the old cartographers' maps are of no use to anyone.
Centuries of petty wars, famines and passing lordlings have followed, and nobody has ever managed to unite {land} under a single banner again.
In the dark centuries that followed, {land} was fought over by barons, brigands and sorcerers, and every generation saw a new master.
Since then life in {land} has been lived day by day, between thin harvests, long winters and ruins best left undisturbed.
Dark years followed, when the laws were forgotten and the word of a gang leader was worth more than any oath.
Since then the villages of {land} have turned inward, each with its own laws, its own shrines and its own grudges.
For generations {land} has been a road for foreign armies, which plundered it without ever wanting to keep it.
Since then nobody has dared to call themselves king in {land}, and those who tried ended up hanging from the battlements of their own castle.
Time has erased almost everything: all that remains in {land} are garbled names, ivy-covered ruins and stories that change with every telling.
legend: It is said that {ruler_il} never died, but sleeps beneath a hill among a host of loyal knights, waiting for the hour of need.
The crown of {ruler_il} was never found: a prophecy says whoever places it on their own head will command the dead of {realm_il}.
Before {realm_il} existed, {land} worshipped {god}, a god of a thousand voices who even now sometimes answers those who call out that name.
A prophecy carved on the gates of the capital foretells that {realm_il} will rise again on the day an heir of {ruler_il} drinks from the silver well.
The sword of {ruler_il}, which never broke nor rusted, was thrown into a lake after the last battle; fishers swear they still see it gleam on moonless nights.
Everyone avoids the ruins of the temple of {god}: it is said the god still sleeps there, dreaming of the end of the world.
{ruler_il} received from {god} a ring that let its wearer speak with animals, and that ring has never been found.
They tell that beneath the capital of {realm_il} lies a second city, identical to the first but upside down, where everything that was lost is still kept.
The bells of {god} will ring three times before the end of the world: two strokes have already been heard, and nobody knows when the third will come.
The heart of {ruler_il} was buried far from the body, in a secret place, and it is said it will keep beating as long as {land} stays free.
{ruler_il} did not die in battle nor of old age, but vanished one night from the highest tower, leaving only a cloak and a letter nobody has ever deciphered.
The priests of {god} kept a book holding the day of death of every inhabitant of {realm_il}; when the temples burned, the book disappeared.
It is said that {god} cursed {ruler_il} for building a palace taller than the god's own temple, and that the curse still falls on the bloodline.
Every hundred years, on the longest night of winter, the army of {realm_il} marches again along the old roads, and whoever meets it must step aside.
The elders swear that {ruler_il} hid the crown's treasure in three different places, and that the map is tattooed on the back of an unwitting descendant.
A prophecy of {god}, repeated by the witches of every village, says that {land} will have a ruler again when the broken tower stands whole once more.
The mirror of {ruler_il} showed whoever looked into it their true enemy; it was stolen on the very night of the burial, and has passed from hand to hand ever since.
cities_intro: Today the cities are few and far between, and each one looks at the others with a mixture of need and suspicion.
Life now huddles in a few walled cities, where people trade, plot and wait for the next disaster.
Power is split between cities that eye each other with suspicion, each with its own lords, its own laws and its own prices.
The few remaining cities are islands of light in a sea of darkness, and whoever travels between them does so at their own risk.
Where great capitals once stood, smaller and tougher cities hold on today, often built with the stones of the old ones.
Today's cities are shelters more than realms: you pay a toll to get in and, sometimes, another one to get out.
Whoever seeks a roof, a market or a judge must find one within the walls of the few surviving cities.
no_city: No city survived: whoever crosses {land} sleeps in the open or among the ruins, and keeps one eye open until dawn.
There is no longer a single city worthy of the name in {land}: only isolated farms, camps and shepherds' huts remain.
The cities of {land} all lie in ruins, and the few inhabitants live in mud villages that move every few years.
Whoever looks for a city in {land} finds only blackened walls and squares overrun by brambles, where at night fires burn that nobody lit.
There are no markets or inns in {land}: to buy salt, iron or news one must wait for the caravans, which come by less and less often.

{name} ({hex}) is in the hands of an old queen who has not left her palace in twenty years, and some doubt she is still alive.

{name} ({hex}) lives in the shadow of a powerful temple, whose priests have more say than the mayor and his guards.
{name} ({hex}) is a town of miners and smiths, rough and welcoming, where every dispute is settled by arm-wrestling.
{name} ({hex}) is ruled by a wizard whose face nobody has ever seen, and whose laws change with every new moon.
{name} ({hex}) hosts the greatest fair in {land}, and once a year everything is sold there, even things that should not exist.
{name} ({hex}) shuts its gates at sunset and opens them for nobody, not even for those who knock crying the name of a relative.

{name} ({hex}) lives in fear of a beast that comes down from the hills every winter, and offers a huge reward to whoever kills it.
{name} ({hex}) is a town of exiles and fugitives, where nobody asks about the past and everyone lies about their name.
{name} ({hex}) has just elected a new burgomaster, and half the town swears the election was bought with foreign gold.

{name} ({hex}) makes the best wine in {land}, and its cellars tempt every brigand in the region.

{name} ({hex}) stands on a disputed ford, and its bridges are watched day and night by guards armed with crossbows.
{name} ({hex}) spreads across both banks, and the two halves of the town have never trusted each other.
{name} ({hex}) charges a toll on every barge that comes up the river, and the boatmen are planning something far from peaceful.

{name} ({hex}) lives on salt and fish, and its sailors swear they have seen things nobody believes.

fortress_intro: Almost all the fortresses of {land} date from the days of {realm_il}, and today they belong to whoever managed to take them.
Stone fortresses still rise on the heights of {land}, some garrisoned, others inhabited by things worse than soldiers.
Whoever holds the fortresses holds the roads, and whoever holds the roads decides who eats and who starves in {land}.
The old fortresses are the last bulwark against the wilds, even if their commanders think more about tolls than about defence.
Towers, keeps and castles dot {land} like the broken teeth of an ancient mouth, and each has a tale of sieges and betrayals.

{name} ({hex}) answers to a castellan who has sworn vengeance on the lords of the cities, and is gathering men and horses.
dungeon_intro: Beneath {land} lie crypts, mines and forgotten temples, and each one keeps a piece of the history of {realm_il}.
The ruins and underground halls of {land} draw adventurers from everywhere: few come back rich, many do not come back at all.
Every village in {land} knows at least one place where nobody should go, and every village has someone who went anyway.
The past of {land} is not buried deep enough: in many places it breaks the surface, and sometimes it moves.
Whoever seeks gold and glory in {land} easily finds a way down; finding the way back up is another matter.

{name} ({hex}): the lair of a sorcerer who sought immortality; nobody knows whether he found it.

sea: The sea washes the shores of {land}, and its fishers tell of islands that come and go with the fog.
Smugglers' coves and the wrecks of ancient ships hide along the coasts of {land}, still laden with goods nobody has claimed.
The sea off {land} is cold and restless, and on stormy nights sailors swear they hear bells ringing beneath the waves.
Merchants, pirates and news of distant lands reach {land} from the sea, and it is often hard to tell which is which.
The cliffs of {land} are dotted with dark lighthouses, and fishers avoid the deep waters where, they say, something enormous sleeps.
rivers: {n} rivers run down from the high ground, and villages, mills and trouble gather along their banks.
{land} is crossed by {n} rivers, each with its own ferryman, its own toll and its own legend.
{n} rivers cut across {land}, and for centuries their fords have been the favourite place for ambushes, fairs and duels.
The waters of {n} rivers flow through {land}, and the boatmen who travel them know every bend, every shoal and every secret of the banks.
{n} rivers wind through {land}, and in their waters fishers sometimes find coins, rings and bones torn from the ruins by the floods.
one_river: A single river crosses {land}, and it is the safest way through: whoever strays from it regrets it.
One great river splits {land} in two, and the folk on either bank speak different dialects and glare at each other.
Only one river waters {land}, and all life clings to its banks: far from the water there is only stone, wind and bones.
A slow, dark river crosses {land}, and the boatmen never travel it at night, for reasons they would rather not explain.
The only river of {land} springs from a source nobody has ever seen, and every spring it carries down objects from an unknown city.
no_river: No river crosses {land}: water comes from deep wells and ancient cisterns, and whoever controls them holds everyone's life in their hands.
No rivers flow in {land}, and every drop of rain is carefully gathered in basins, waterskins and channels cut into the rock.
{land} has no rivers, but the old folk say there was once one, and that a curse drained it dry.
Without rivers, {land} lives on springs and wells, and quarrels over water are fiercer than those over gold.
factions_intro: Today several factions vie for power in {land}, and two of them matter more than all the rest.
No king rules {land}, but the void left by the crown has been filled by greedy and ambitious factions.
Whoever wants to do business in {land} must know whom to pay, whom to obey and whom never to turn their back on.
Behind every toll, every hanging and every feast in {land} there is the hand of one of its factions.
The true powers of {land} do not sit on a throne, but in secret halls, smoky inns and camps in the woods.
In {land} power is not inherited: it is bought, stolen or won by the sword, and today it rests in few hands.
Among the ruins of what was once {realm_il}, new forces are stirring today, determined to seize whatever is left.
faction: {fac_il} brings together the richest merchants of {land}, and wants to reopen the old trade roads at any cost.
{fac_il} was born among the veterans of a forgotten war, and today sells its swords to anyone who can pay.
{fac_il} guards the secrets of the wizards of {realm_il}, and lets nobody study them without its leave.
{fac_il} preaches the return of the old god {god}, and gathers followers among the poor, the sick and the desperate of every village.
{fac_il} claims descent from {ruler_il}, and asserts the right to rule {land} in the name of the old crown.
{fac_il} controls the smuggling of salt, weapons and relics, and has ears in every inn and every harbour.
{fac_il} hunts witches, monsters and the undead, but its methods are said to frighten the peasants more than the beasts themselves.
{fac_il} gathers the thieves, beggars and cutpurses of the cities, and enforces its own rules where the guards cannot reach.
{fac_il} wants to return {land} to the wild, and sabotages mills, bridges and roads in the name of the forest spirits.
{fac_il} has sought the pieces of the seal of {realm_il} for generations, and already holds more of them than it admits.
{fac_il} lends money to lords and villages, and collects its debts with endless patience and even greater cruelty.
{fac_il} protects travellers on the roads in exchange for a toll, and whoever refuses to pay soon learns what they were being protected from.
{fac_il} is led by a blind seer, and makes every decision by reading the flight of crows and the entrails of fish.
{fac_il} recruits young people in the poorest villages, promising lands and titles in a kingdom yet to be born.
{fac_il} studies the ruins and underground places of {land}, and pays adventurers well for books, maps and strange objects.
{fac_il} controls the mines and forges of {land}, and decides who may buy weapons and who must make do with sticks.
{fac_il} was founded to avenge the fall of {realm_il}, and after centuries it still has not decided whom to blame.
{fac_il} is feared all over {land} for its assassins, who never miss their mark and never leave witnesses.
{fac_il} runs the inns and coaching stations along the roads, and always knows who is travelling, with whom and with how much money.
rivalry: {fac1_il} and {fac2_il} have hated each other for three generations, and by now nobody remembers who started it.
{fac1_il} and {fac2_il} fight openly in the streets, but in secret their leaders meet at every new moon.
{fac1_il} owes a huge sum to {fac2_il}, and the day of reckoning is approaching with no gold to settle the debt.
A marriage should soon unite the leaders of {fac1_il} and {fac2_il}, but many on both sides would do anything to stop it.
{fac1_il} accuses {fac2_il} of murdering its old leader, and has sworn revenge publicly, before a hundred witnesses.
{fac1_il} and {fac2_il} have signed a fragile truce, which holds only out of fear of a common enemy.
{fac1_il} has planted its spies in the ranks of {fac2_il}, and knows every move before it is even decided.
{fac1_il} and {fac2_il} are after the same lost treasure, but the map to find it is torn in two, and each holds one half.
{fac1_il} and {fac2_il} were once a single faction, and their split was so bloody that nobody likes to speak of it.
{fac1_il} secretly holds a valuable hostage from {fac2_il}, and uses that hostage to get whatever it wants without ever raising its voice.
{fac1_il} scorns {fac2_il} in public, but every month it secretly buys weapons, poisons and information from it.
{fac1_il} and {fac2_il} have split {land} into two spheres of influence, and whoever crosses the line is found in a ditch at dawn.
{fac1_il} swore allegiance to {fac2_il} after a humiliating defeat, but is only waiting for the right moment to betray that oath.
now_intro: Now, though, something is changing, and even the most stubborn folk of {land} are starting to notice.
But the fragile peace of {land} is about to end, and the signs are now plain for everyone to see.
In recent months, though, the inns of {land} have been whispering about one thing only.
This year winter came early, and with the frost came something nobody can yet put a name to.
Lately, though, the elders of {land} shake their heads and say the worst is yet to come.
Now a new danger threatens {land}, and the old rivalries may soon seem a small matter.
Things never stay still for long in {land}, and this time too a storm is brewing far from prying eyes.
But ever since this spring began, nothing in {land} has gone the way it should.
And it is right now, while the powerful squabble over crumbs, that the gravest threat in centuries is gathering over {land}.
threat: An orc army gathers at the borders, and its scouts have already been seen prowling the high ground.
A sickness that turns the eyes grey spreads from village to village, and the healers do not know where it comes from.
Crops no longer grow near the old ruins, and animals flee towards the lowlands for no reason.
A dragon has been seen flying low over {land}, and since then the flocks have vanished one after another.
An heir of {realm_il} has reappeared and claims {land}, with a seal few can dispute and an army that grows every day.
The bells of a buried temple ring at night, and whoever hears them always dreams the same dream.
The dead of the old battlefields have started walking again, and every night they come a little closer to the villages.
The cult of {god} has secretly been reborn, and its faithful are kidnapping travellers for a rite that must be completed at the next solstice.
A horde of raiders, driven from their own lands by something worse, is sweeping down on {land}, burning everything in its path.
A mad wizard has taken over a forgotten tower, and since then the sky over {land} has changed colour every night.
The spring the largest villages depend on is drying up, and whoever controls the remaining water will be able to dictate terms to everyone.
A foreign army, led by a general said to be invincible, has crossed the borders and demands the surrender of every city.
Something has woken beneath the mountains: the earth shakes every night, and warm water tasting of iron rises from the wells.
A pack of werewolves hunts the countryside of {land}, and some say their leader sits on a town council by day.
The tomb of {ruler_il} has been desecrated, and whoever did it took away something that should have stayed buried forever.
An unnatural fog creeps forward a few paces every day, and the villages it swallows send no more news.
A giant come down from the glaciers has made a home in an old fortress, and demands a tribute of cattle from every village in the valley.
A slow poison has begun killing the powerful of {land} one after another, and each side blames its rivals.
The stars above {land} have shifted, and the astrologers announce that the return of {god} is a matter of weeks.
A gold fever has swept {land}: they say gold is surfacing from the ground in a remote valley, and every desperate soul is rushing there.
The gates of a dwarven fortress, shut for centuries, have opened again, but what comes out of them is not dwarves.
omen: For three nights the moon has risen blood-red, and the dogs howl without pause until dawn.
The statues of {ruler_il} in the village squares have begun to weep black tears.
Three-legged chicks are hatching in the henhouses, and the village witches refuse to say what it means.
The flocks of crows all fly in the same direction, and nobody has ever seen them come back.
In every well of {land} the water turned salty on the same day, at the same hour.
A green-tailed comet has been crossing the sky for weeks, and the astrologers have stopped leaving their homes.
The children of {land} sing in their sleep a rhyme nobody taught them, in a language dead for centuries.
In a single night a chalk mark appeared on the doors of the houses: the forgotten symbol of {god}.
Wine sours in the barrels, milk curdles in the pails and candles go out by themselves as soon as darkness falls.
An old banner of {realm_il}, buried for centuries, has been seen flying from the highest tower in {land}, and nobody knows who raised it.
The bees have abandoned their hives and the fish swim the wrong way up the streams, as if fleeing something.
Every night the old folk all dream of the same bronze door, and wake with their hands covered in earth.
All across {land} the bells rang by themselves at midnight, thirteen strokes, and then fell silent.
An eclipse no astronomer had foreseen darkened the sun for a whole hour, and since then the horses refuse to leave their stables.
A dying pilgrim reached the nearest village repeating a single name, always the same: that of {ruler_il}.

forest: Forests cover much of {land}: old, thick, and full of paths that lead nowhere.
Creatures older than humankind still live in the woods of {land}, and woodcutters leave offerings of bread before felling a tree.
The forests of {land} hide whole cities among their trees, swallowed by roots in a few centuries of neglect.
Whoever enters the forests of {land} without a guide soon loses the path, and sometimes the memory of how they got there.
hills: The hills of {land} are dotted with barrows and fallen towers, and shepherds avoid the hilltops.
Among the hills of {land} hide narrow valleys and isolated villages, where strangers are greeted with bread and watched with suspicion.
The hills of {land} are riddled with old mines, and at night the sound of picks nobody wields echoes from the abandoned tunnels.
Rings of standing stones crown the hills of {land}, and the shepherds swear the stones change places from one year to the next.
mountains: The mountains of {land} are high and cold, and their passes stay closed half of the year.
Narrow passes and ancient glaciers open among the mountains of {land}, and sometimes motionless figures can be glimpsed in the ice, as if watching.
The mountains of {land} are rich in iron and silver, and the dwarves who once mined them have never accepted their loss.
Eagles as big as horses nest on the peaks of {land}, and the mountain folk know that whoever steals an egg never comes back down.
